Naval Ravikant once shared a story about Elon Musk confronting Bill Gates after learning that Gates had shorted Tesla, a position amounting to roughly 1% of Tesla’s total shares

Over time, that bet may have already cost Gates more than $10 billion. If Tesla becomes the world’s most valuable company by a wide margin, that short position will bankrupt even Bill Gates

Musk was genuinely confused. How could someone who publicly championed clean energy bet against a company that was actively building it?

Gates reportedly described it as “just a financial move.” But for Musk, it was never about money

According to Naval, that moment revealed something fundamental about Elon Musk. He is not driven by status or wealth, he is driven by purpose. The billions he earns are not trophies, they are tools. Tools to build rockets, electric vehicles, and a future beyond Earth

Source: @ScottAdamsSays, @naval
